slides.title: Your first 30 days as an analyst, ~planned~
Week 1: ~learn~ the data
rows: Get access: email, Excel, SQL client, BI tool, shared drive
You can open every file your team talks about
Ask for the last 3 reports your team sent
You know what the team ships every week
Find where each report's numbers come from
You can name the source table or file for each
Write a glossary: every short form you hear
MTD, GMV, TAT, churn all have a one-line meaning
Sit with whoever makes the main report
You have watched it built once, start to end
Note the 5 numbers your manager looks at first
You know what matters before you build anything
Week-end note to your manager: what you learnt
Five lines, no slides, sent on Friday

slides.title: Week 2: ~own~ one report
rows: Take over one small recurring report
Your name is on it from this week
Rebuild it once, slowly, by hand
Your total matches last week's version
Write the steps in a text file
Someone else could run it from your notes
Add 3 checks: row count, total, blanks
You catch a broken file before your manager does
Send it before the deadline, not on it
It reaches them a few hours early
Ask: what do you do with this report?
You know the decision it feeds
Fix one small thing people complain about
One column, label or sort order is better

slides.title: Week 3: ~speed~ it up
rows: Time each step of your report
You know which step eats the most minutes
Replace copy-paste with formulas or a pivot
The slowest manual step is gone
Turn the raw data into an Excel Table
New rows flow into formulas and pivots
Save your SQL queries in one file with comments
You can rerun any pull in a minute
Learn the 10 shortcuts you use most
Mouse trips go down every day
Ask a senior to review one of your queries
You get one better way of writing it
Document what changed and why
The next person is not confused

slides.title: Week 4: your first ~insight~
rows: Pick one number that moved this month
You know which number and by how much
Break it down by region, product or channel
You know where the change came from
Check it is real: data error or real change?
You have ruled out a broken file
Write it in 3 lines: what, why, so what
A busy manager gets it in 20 seconds
Show it to your manager before anyone else
No surprises in a team meeting
Add it to your report as a small note
Your report now says something, not only shows
Ask for feedback on your first month
You know one thing to keep and one to fix

slides.title: Days 29 and 30: ~set up~ month two
rows: List what you own, what you shadow, what you skip
Your work is clear to you and your manager
Pick one skill your team uses that you lack
Month two has one learning goal
Keep a wins file: date, task, result
Your appraisal writes itself later

slides.title: Day 1 is ~closer~ than you think.
